title: Hotfix: fix metric cardinality regression in overload events
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Fixes unintended high-cardinality labels on overload/shed metrics introduced during hot-route protection rollout. No customer-visible behavior change; metrics/dashboards become stable again.
body: Context: During the hot-route capacity protection rollout we introduced new overload event metrics (shed/admission_control) that were intended to be low-cardinality (route_group, tier, region, reason). In the last merge window we accidentally started emitting per-request / per-tenant labels on the overload event counters due to a tag plumbing change in the gateway -> telemetry bridge. This caused a rapid increase in series count in Prometheus and intermittent ingestion backpressure, and it also made the SRE dashboards noisy/slow to load. What changed: (1) Add a strict label allowlist for overload event metrics in the telemetry emitter and drop/ignore all non-allowed labels (e.g., tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, api_key_id, user_agent, model_revision). (2) Split the old overloaded "overload_event" into two metrics: redwood_overload_shed_total and redwood_overload_admission_denied_total with a stable label set {route_group, tier, region, reason}. (3) Add a lightweight counter redwood_overload_labels_dropped_total{metric_name,label_key} to make future regressions visible without paging the fleet. (4) Update dashboard queries to use the new metrics and remove the accidental group-by on tenant_id. Notes: This is intentionally conservative and enforces invariants close to the emitter to avoid future regressions from upstream tag propagation. This does not change overload behavior itself; only metric emission. Validation: Verified in staging by replaying overload simulation traffic and confirming series count stays flat; production canary (us-east) shows series count returning to baseline within ~30 minutes after rollout. Checklist: [x] Unit tests for allowlist behavior + label drop accounting [x] Update dashboards/recording rules in monorepo bundle [x] Backwards-compat shim: keep the old metric name as an alias for 7 days (deprecated) to avoid alert breakage during rollout [x] Added runbook note: "If series count spikes, check labels_dropped_total". Rollout plan: Merge + deploy with standard gateway release train; no flag required. Monitoring: prometheus_remote_write_queue, series_count by job=telemetry, and the hot-route protection dashboards (ENG-4926).
commits: telemetry: add label allowlist + dropped-label accounting for overload metrics
metrics: split overload_event into shed/admission metrics with stable label set
dashboards: update hot-route protection panels/recording rules to new metric names
tests: add regression coverage for high-cardinality tag propagation
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we guarantee we never re-introduce tenant_id via shared context tags? The code path currently merges request-scoped tags by default in a couple places.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yep — this change applies the allowlist at the last possible step (right before emit). Even if upstream merges request context tags, they’ll be dropped for these metric names. Added a unit test that simulates request tags containing tenant_id/request_id/trace_id to ensure they never make it through.

Allison Grant (review): Please keep naming consistent with the metrics standard doc: *_total suffix and reason label values should be stable enums. Also avoid label_key cardinality explosion in labels_dropped_total.

Nadia Rahman (author): Updated metric names to *_total and normalized reason values to the existing enum set (quota, overload, capacity, circuit_open, unknown). For labels_dropped_total, label_key is limited to a small allowlist of known-problem keys (tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, api_key_id, user_agent, model_revision) to keep it bounded.
Rafael Mendes (review): For SRE: will this break existing alerts today? We had a paging storm risk if panels fail to load during an event.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added a 7-day alias gauge/counter mapping (old name emits the same value with the same stable labels) and updated dashboards/recording rules in this PR. Alerts should continue to work immediately, but they’ll use the new rules once deployed.
Caleb Johnson (review): Any evidence this fixes remote_write lag? Also, can we add a note to the runbook on how to confirm cardinality is back to baseline?

Nadia Rahman (author): Added staging evidence to the PR description and included a runbook snippet pointing to series_count{job="api-gateway"} and top label keys via promtool/cardinality panel; also added labels_dropped_total to the dashboard so on-call can confirm the guardrail is working.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main; deployed in the next gateway release train (us-east then eu-west).
